questions.prompt: Your teacher writes the word "excursion" on the board and asks where the strong beat falls. Which line marks the stress in the right place?
questions.explanation: "ex-CUR-sion" is right: the word has three beats and the strong one falls in the middle, because a word ending in -sion is always stressed on the syllable just before that ending. "EX-cur-sion" hits the first beat, which is where English stresses most short nouns but not this one. "ex-cur-SION" hits the ending itself, and -sion is never stressed in English. And "ex-cur-si-ON" cuts the word into four beats the way French does, whereas English says -sion in one single beat.

questions.prompt: A journalist interviews Nizar, a young goalkeeper from Bizerte, and asks him: "How do you feel about your first season with the club?" Which of these answers fits the question?

options.text: Since I signed the contract in June.
I am delighted with it, honestly.
Because the coach trusted me early.

questions.explanation: "I am delighted with it, honestly." is the one: How do you feel about…? asks a player whether he is satisfied or not, and the answer names the feeling — delighted, pleased, disappointed, fed up. "Since I signed the contract in June." gives a starting point, so it answers How long…? or Since when…?; "About four hundred supporters came." gives a number, so it answers How many…?; and "Because the coach trusted me early." gives a reason, so it answers Why…?

questions.prompt: Read this notice at a youth hostel in Tabarka: "Diving — Monday and Thursday, 9 a.m. Canoeing — Monday and Friday, 3 p.m. Windsurfing — every day except Monday, 4 p.m. Sailing — Wednesday, 10 a.m." Wassim is free only on Monday afternoon. What can he do?
questions.explanation: "He can go canoeing." is right: canoeing is the only activity that passes both tests at once — it is offered on Monday, and it starts at 3 p.m., which is the afternoon. "He can go diving." fails on the second test only: diving is indeed on Monday, but at 9 a.m., when Wassim is not free. "He can go windsurfing." fails on the first: the notice offers it every day except Monday. And "He can go sailing." moves the reader to Wednesday, a day that is not Wassim's.

questions.prompt: Sofien writes to his cousin about a family holiday: "My brother didn't enjoy the crossing to Sicily, ___" Which ending completes his sentence in correct English?

options.text: and I didn't enjoy it either.
and I didn't enjoy it too.
and neither I didn't enjoy it.
and I didn't enjoy it neither.

questions.explanation: "and I didn't enjoy it either." is right: the first half of the sentence is negative, and the word that adds a second negative fact at the end of a sentence is either. "and I didn't enjoy it too." uses too, which only works when the sentence is affirmative — My brother enjoyed it and I enjoyed it too. "and I didn't enjoy it neither." negates twice, since neither already carries its own negative and didn't is there as well. And "and neither I didn't enjoy it." makes the same double negative and forgets that after neither the auxiliary jumps in front of the subject: neither did I.

questions.prompt: Put the word in brackets in the right form: "A year abroad will ___ anybody's view of the world. (broad)"
questions.explanation: "broaden" is right: after will the sentence needs a verb in its base form, and the verb built on the adjective broad is broaden, with the ending -en that also gives widen, shorten and strengthen. "broadly" is an adverb, and an adverb cannot be the verb of the sentence. "broader" is the comparative adjective, which would need a noun after it. And "broadness" is a noun, so the sentence would be left with will and no verb at all.
